chapter.li: Verse28 And when he had thus spoken, he went before, ascending up to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse29 And it came to pass, when he had come near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples, VerseEnd Verse30 saying, Go into the village ahead of you, in which, at your entering, you shall find a colt tied, on which man never yet sat; untie him and bring him to me. VerseEnd Verse31 And if any man ask you, Why do you untie the colt? — thus shall you say unto him: Because the Lord has need of him. VerseEnd

Verse32 And they who were sent went their way and found even as he had said unto them. VerseEnd Verse33 And as they were untying the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why do you untie the colt? VerseEnd Verse34 And they said, The Lord has need of him. VerseEnd Verse35 And they brought him to Jesus, and they cast their garments upon the colt, and they seated Jesus thereon. VerseEnd Verse36 And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way. VerseEnd

Verse37 And when he had come near, even now at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen, VerseEnd Verse38 saying, Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord; peace in Heaven and glory in the highest. VerseEnd Verse39 And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke your disciples. VerseEnd Verse40 And he answered and said unto them, If these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out. VerseEnd

Verse41 And when he had come near, he beheld the city and wept over it, VerseEnd Verse42 saying, If you had known, even you, at least in this your day, the things which belong unto your peace; but now they are hidden from your eyes. VerseEnd Verse43 For the days shall come upon you that your enemies shall cast a trench about you, and encompass you round, and keep you in on every side, VerseEnd Verse44 and shall lay you even with the ground, and your children within you. And they shall not leave in you one stone upon another, because you knew not the time of your visitation. VerseEnd

Verse45 And he went into the temple and began to cast out them who sold therein and them who bought, VerseEnd Verse46 saying unto them, It is written: My house is a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of thieves. VerseEnd Verse47 And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests, and the scribes, and the chief of the people sought to destroy him, VerseEnd Verse48 and could not find what they might do, for all the people were very attentive to hear him. VerseEnd

LEChapter20 Verse1 And it came to pass that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders VerseEnd Verse2 and spoke unto him, saying, Tell us by what authority you do these things; or who is he who gave you this authority? VerseEnd Verse3 And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; answer me: VerseEnd Verse4 The baptism of John, was it from Heaven or of men? VerseEnd Verse5 And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From Heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him? VerseEnd Verse6 And if we say, Of men, all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet. VerseEnd Verse7 And they answered that they could not tell from where it was. VerseEnd Verse8 Jesus said unto them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do those things. VerseEnd

Verse9 Then began he to speak to the people this parable: A certain man planted a vineyard, and leased it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time. VerseEnd Verse10 And at the season of the harvest, he sent his servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard; but the husbandmen beat him and sent him away empty. VerseEnd Verse11 And again he sent another servant, and they beat him also, and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty. VerseEnd Verse12 And again he sent a third, and they wounded him also and cast him out. VerseEnd Verse13 Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; it may be they will reverence him when they see him. VerseEnd Verse14 But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours. VerseEnd Verse15 So they cast him out of the vineyard and killed him. What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do unto them? VerseEnd Verse16 He shall come and destroy these husbandmen and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard this, they said, God forbid. VerseEnd

Verse17 And he beheld them and said, What is this then which is written: The stone which the builders rejected, the same has become the head of the corner? VerseEnd Verse18 Whoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken, but on whomever it shall fall, it shall grind him to powder. VerseEnd Verse19 And the chief priests and the scribes, the same hour, sought to lay hands on him, but they feared the people, for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them. VerseEnd

Verse20 And they watched him and sent forth spies who should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so doing they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor. VerseEnd Verse21 And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that you say and teach rightly, neither regard the person of any, but teach the way of God truly. VerseEnd Verse22 Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar? Or no? VerseEnd Verse23 But he perceived their craftiness and said unto them, Why do you test me? VerseEnd Verse24 Show me a penny. Whose image and superscription has it? They answered and said, Caesar’s. VerseEnd Verse25 And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s and unto God the things which are God’s. VerseEnd Verse26 And they could not catch him in his words before the people, and they marveled at his answer and held their peace. VerseEnd

Verse27 Then came unto him certain of the Sadducees, who deny that there is any resurrection, and they asked him, VerseEnd Verse28 saying, Master, Moses wrote unto us, saying if any man’s brother die having a wife and he die without children, that his brother should take his wife and raise up seed unto his brother. VerseEnd Verse29 There were therefore seven brethren. The first took a wife and died without children. VerseEnd Verse30 And the second took her to wife and he died childless. VerseEnd Verse31 And the third took her in like manner, and the seven also, and they left no children and died. VerseEnd Verse32 And last of all the woman died also. VerseEnd Verse33 Therefore, in the resurrection, whose wife of them is she? For seven had her to wife. VerseEnd Verse34 And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry and are given in marriage, VerseEnd Verse35 but they who shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world through resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage, VerseEnd Verse36 neither can they die anymore, for they are equal unto the angels and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection. VerseEnd Verse37 Now, that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. VerseEnd Verse38 For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living, for all live unto him. VerseEnd Verse39 Then certain of the scribes answering said, Master, you have well said. VerseEnd Verse40 And after that, they dare not ask him any question at all. VerseEnd

Verse41 And he said unto them, How do they say that Christ is David’s son? VerseEnd Verse42 And David himself said in the book of Psalms, The Lord said unto my lord, Sit on my right hand VerseEnd Verse43 until I make your enemies your footstool. VerseEnd Verse44 David therefore calls him Lord; how is he then his son? VerseEnd

Verse45 Then in the audience of all the people he said unto his disciples, VerseEnd Verse46 Beware of the scribes who desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts, VerseEnd Verse47 who devour widows’ houses and for a show make long prayers; the same shall receive greater damnation. VerseEnd

LEChapter21 Verse1 And he looked up and saw the rich men casting in their gifts into the treasury. VerseEnd Verse2 And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in there two mites. VerseEnd Verse3 And he said, Truly I say unto you that this poor widow has cast in more than they all, for all VerseEnd Verse4 these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God, but she of her poverty has cast in all the possessions that she had. VerseEnd

Verse5 And as some spoke of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said, VerseEnd Verse6 These things which you behold, the days will come in which there shall not be left one stone upon another which shall not be thrown down. VerseEnd Verse7 And the disciples asked him, saying, Master, when shall these things be? And what sign will you show when these things shall come to pass? VerseEnd

Verse8 And he said, The time draws near, and therefore take heed, that you should be not deceived, for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; go not therefore after them. VerseEnd Verse9 And when you shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified, for these things must first come to pass; but this is not the end. VerseEnd Verse10 Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, VerseEnd Verse11 and great earthquakes shall be in diverse places, and famines, and pestilences, and fearful sights, and great signs shall there be from Heaven. VerseEnd Verse12 But before all these things shall come, they shall lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake. VerseEnd Verse14 Settle this therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what you shall answer, VerseEnd Verse15 for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries shall not be able to refute nor resist, VerseEnd Verse13 and it shall turn to you for a testimony. VerseEnd Verse16 And you shall be betrayed, both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death. VerseEnd Verse17 And you shall be hated of all the world for my name’s sake. VerseEnd Verse18 But there shall not a hair of your head perish. VerseEnd Verse19 In your patience, possess your souls. VerseEnd

Verse20 And when you shall see Jerusalem encompassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is near. VerseEnd Verse21 Then let them who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and let them who are in the midst of it depart out, and let not them who are in the countries return to enter into the city; VerseEnd Verse22 for these are the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. VerseEnd Verse23 But woe unto them who are with child, and to them who give suck in those days, for there shall be great distress in the land and wrath upon this people, VerseEnd Verse24 and they shall fall by the edge of the sword and shall be led away captive into all nations. And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled. Now these things he spoke unto them concerning the destruction of Jerusalem. VerseEnd

Verse25 And then his disciples asked him, saying, Master, tell us concerning your coming. And he answered them and said, In the generation in which the times of the Gentiles shall be fulfilled, there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars, and upon the earth, distress of nations with perplexity, like the sea and the waves roaring. The earth also shall be troubled, and the waters of the great deep, VerseEnd Verse26 men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth, for the Powers of Heaven shall be shaken; VerseEnd Verse28 and when these things begin to come to pass, then look up and lift up your heads, for the day of your redemption draws near. VerseEnd Verse27 And then shall they see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. VerseEnd

Verse29 And he spoke to them a parable, saying, Behold the fig tree and all the trees; VerseEnd Verse30 when they now shoot forth, you see and know of your own selves that summer is now near at hand. VerseEnd Verse31 So likewise you, when you see these things come to pass, know that the kingdom of God is near at hand. VerseEnd Verse32 Truly I say unto you, this generation — the generation when the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled — shall not pass away until all are fulfilled. VerseEnd Verse33 Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. VerseEnd Verse34 Let my disciples therefore take heed to themselves, lest at any time their hearts should be burdened with overindulgence, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day come upon them unawares; VerseEnd Verse35 for as a snare it shall come on all them who dwell on the face of the whole earth. VerseEnd Verse36 And what I say unto one, I say unto all. Watch, therefore, and pray always, and keep my commandments, that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things which shall come to pass and to stand before the Son of Man when he shall come, clothed in the glory of his Father. VerseEnd

Verse37 And in the daytime, he was teaching in the temple; and at night, he went out and stayed the night in the mount that is called Olives. VerseEnd Verse38 And the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him. VerseEnd
